name: Galera Cluster
tagline: Synchronous multi-primary replication for MySQL and MariaDB, now owned by MariaDB plc.
description: Galera Cluster is a write-set replication (wsrep) library plus patched MySQL/MariaDB servers that turn a group of nodes into a virtually synchronous multi-primary cluster. Transactions execute locally, then their write-sets are broadcast and certified in a global order, which yields no lost commits on failover and consistent data on every node. Codership, the Finnish company behind it, was acquired by MariaDB plc in 2025; the library continues to power MariaDB Galera, Percona XtraDB Cluster and Codership's own MySQL builds. Treat it as an HA technology for 3-5 node clusters rather than a way to scale writes.

pricing.notes: Library and community builds are GPLv2; Galera Enterprise and support are sold through MariaDB.

scale.notes: Every node stores and applies all data; adding nodes adds read capacity and resilience, not write capacity.

strengths: Certification-based replication gives zero committed-data loss on node failure
True multi-primary: any node can take writes
Parallel applier threads keep replicas close to real time
Automatic state transfer when nodes join or rejoin
Bundled with MariaDB and Percona, so widely packaged
weaknesses: Write latency bounded by the slowest node round-trip
Conflicting writes from different nodes surface as deadlocks at commit
Schema changes via TOI block the cluster; RSU requires care
InnoDB only; MyISAM and some features are unsupported
useCases: Geographically spread read replicas with consistent data
Active-active setups behind a load balancer such as MaxScale or ProxySQL
